name: Kharif (Monsoon Season)
climate_characteristics: Warm, humid, accounts for 80-85% of annual rainfall in Bihar via South-West Monsoon.

satellite_signatures.ndvi_pattern: Rapid green-up in July-August, peak vegetative cover (NDVI 0.65-0.85) in September, senescence in October.
satellite_signatures.soil_moisture_pattern: Elevated surface soil moisture (SMAP > 0.30 m³/m³), flood inundation detectable in Northern floodplains.

key_hazards: Erratic monsoon onset delay (late nursery transplanting)
Prolonged dry spells (monsoon breaks) causing vegetative drought
Severe flooding in Kosi, Gandak, Bagmati, Mahananda basins (North Bihar)
Waterlogging in flat lowlands (Tal and Diara lands)

source_notes.meteorology: India Meteorological Department (IMD) Monsoon Climatology of Bihar.
source_notes.agriculture: Department of Agriculture, Government of Bihar: Kharif Season Calendar.

name: Rabi (Winter Season)
climate_characteristics: Cool, dry conditions with occasional light showers from Western Disturbances (15-40 mm total rain).

satellite_signatures.ndvi_pattern: Crop emergence in December, peak greenness (NDVI 0.55-0.75) in late January - February, yellowing in March.
satellite_signatures.soil_moisture_pattern: Declining profile moisture; crop relies heavily on residual monsoon moisture and tubewell irrigation.

key_hazards: Terminal heat stress: rapid spikes in maximum temperatures (>32-35°C) in late February / early March during wheat grain filling, reducing thousand-grain weight
Cold wave / ground frost in late December / early January affecting mustard and potato
Groundwater table decline in non-alluvial South Bihar tracts

source_notes.heat_stress: ICAR-IIWBR / CIMMYT CSISA heat vulnerability studies in Eastern IGP.

name: Zaid (Summer Season)
climate_characteristics: Intensely hot and dry, high evaporative demand (ET > 7-9 mm/day), high solar irradiance, westerly winds (Loo).

satellite_signatures.ndvi_pattern: Widespread bare-field signal (NDVI < 0.20) across >80% of cropland unless irrigated catch crop (moong, vegetables) is sown.
satellite_signatures.soil_moisture_pattern: Severe surface dry-down (SMAP < 0.10 m³/m³), strong positive LST anomalies.

key_hazards: Bare field vulnerability: exposed topsoil subject to wind erosion and high-heat solar oxidation of organic matter
Acute water table depression and high pumping fuel/electricity costs

source_notes.climatology: NASA POWER Agroclimatology & IMD State Climate Summary.
source_notes.bare_soil: Sentinel-2 / Landsat NDVI seasonal dynamics in Bihar.
